blogs.title: The Pulmonary Mask: When Recurrent Pleural Effusions Hide a Pancreatic Secret
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic trap of Pancreatopleural Fistula (PPF), where patients present exclusively with respiratory distress, chest pain, and massive pleural effusions while lacking classic abdominal symptoms. We will analyze why clinicians often exhaust pulmonary workups (including empiric TB treatment) before considering an intra-abdominal source, and highlight the critical historical clue—blunt abdominal trauma—that unlocked the diagnosis in this pediatric case.

blogs.title: Beyond ADA and Cytology: Interpreting Hemorrhagic, Amylase-Rich Pleural Fluid
blogs.description: Focusing on the laboratory dilemma, this article dissects the interpretation of pleural fluid analysis in complex effusions. We will compare the differential diagnosis for hemorrhagic fluid with elevated Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) versus markedly elevated amylase/lipase. Key teaching points include distinguishing pancreatic-type amylase from salivary-type amylase to rule out esophageal perforation or malignancy, and establishing the pathognomonic threshold (>1000 IU/L) that should immediately trigger a pancreatic workup.

blogs.title: Mapping the Leak: Choosing Between CT, MRCP, and ERCP for Suspected PPF
blogs.description: Imaging is often the bottleneck in diagnosing PPF. This post evaluates the sensitivity and specific utility of different modalities based on current literature and this case report. We will discuss why Contrast-Enhanced CT may identify the tract but miss the fistula itself, why MRCP is the preferred non-invasive tool for visualizing ductal anatomy and fistulous tracts, and when to escalate to ERCP not just for diagnosis, but as a definitive therapeutic bridge.

blogs.title: Conservative First? Navigating Medical vs. Endoscopic Management of Pediatric PPF
blogs.description: With no standardized guidelines for pediatric PPF, this post analyzes the tension between initial conservative management (NPO, TPN, Octreotide) and early endoscopic intervention. Using data from this case (successful medical closure in 10 days) against broader literature showing low success rates for保守 therapy in children (<12%), we will outline a decision-making algorithm for when to start somatostatin analogues versus when to proceed directly to ERCP stenting or surgical diversion.

blogs.title: Handlebar Hernias and Hidden Trauma: The Unique Etiology of Pediatric Pancreatitis
blogs.description: While adult PPF is overwhelmingly driven by alcohol-induced chronic pancreatitis, pediatric cases have a distinctly different etiologic profile. This post contrasts adult vs. pediatric causes, focusing on blunt abdominal trauma (e.g., bicycle handlebars) and genetic predispositions (PRSS1, SPINK1 mutations). It serves as a reminder to screen for occult trauma in children presenting with 'idiopathic' pancreatitis or unexplained effusions, especially when social factors like fear of bullying may delay history taking.
